description: DG-6 over-decisiveness — GROUNDED partial resolution: per-battle combat-effectiveness (CEV) friction. Jordan directive 2026-07-22 ('validate emergent results top-down from historical precedent; extend code as required to resolve standing issues using academic research, military theory, mathematics, historical precedent'). Root cause CONFIRMED (mathematical): melee attrition sums N independent per-soldier dice -> CV self-averages ~1/sqrt(N) (measured 0.89->0.06 for N=4->1024); pool scales linearly with troops -> compute_degree near-deterministic from the force ratio -> outcomes collapse to 100%/0% where history shows bands. Fix (two research passes, ~200k tokens; grounding in audit/2026-07-22-mass-battle-stress-test/dg6_friction_resolution.md): keep the self-averaging attrition core, add a per-BATTLE, per-side multiplicative CEV factor M ~ LogNormal(0, sigma^2) drawn ONCE per battle (orchestration._draw_friction_cev, lazy so multi-turn re-entries keep the single draw), multiplying the subunit combat pool (core/exchange). Law of total variance: the attrition term ->0 with N (kept), the once-per-battle shock stays O(1) -> scale-invariant outcome variance (Dupuy CEV / Clausewitz friction / stochastic-Lanchester; Kingman 2002, Beyerchen 1992, Rowland, Sabin Lost Battles). CALIBRATED gauge-INDEPENDENTLY to the Dupuy DLEDB force-ratio win-curve (NOT the gauge, I5): sigma=1.1 reproduces 1.2:1->57% (t55), 1.5:1->62% (t62), 2:1->70% (t70), 3:1->82% (t80). Mechanism verified (test_friction_cev.py, 7): default-inert/byte-exact off; drawn once per battle not per turn; large-force 2:1 collapses to >=95% without friction and stays banded <90% with it (the scale-invariant-variance fix); I1/I2 hold. HONEST FINDING -- friction is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT, ships DEFAULT OFF: the 20-row history gauge moves 6/20 -> 4/20 with uniform friction ON, because (1) envelopment rows (H3/H4) stay ~100% -- their over-decisiveness is STRUCTURAL (envelopment geometry), needing a CONJUNCTIVE gate (Goldsworthy/Sabin: center-holds x cavalry-sufficiency x terrain), not symmetric noise; (2) friction BREAKS the Stage E brace repel (C2/C6 REPELLED->NOT-REPELLED: a big CEV draw lets cavalry break a braced line, but Waterloo-squares repel is near-deterministic) -- friction must be exempted/damped in the brace repel; (3) near-parity rows pushed just out of band. So it ships gated OFF (byte-exact, inert; grid oracle unaffected -- I4). Complete DG-6 resolution = (a) this CEV friction + (b) conjunctive envelopment gate + (c) brace-repel preservation -- scoped as follow-on. needs_jordan: default-flip + the (b)/(c) design calls. No constant tuned to the gauge.

A2 (perception-limited order conditions): core/contact.py's _visible_enemy_cells filters the enemy_range: order trigger through a facing cone (FOV_HALF_DEG, composed on the existing MB_FACING_MODEL/MB_FACING_FOV_GATE flags after a round-2 fix -- round 1 ran unconditionally). A6 (missile ammunition and resupply): Subunit.eff_volleys/drain_volleys/resupply_volleys, mirroring stamina's own per-subunit, own-else-inherited-Unit ledger exactly. Round 1 put this on percell._ColBlock (column-block granularity); round 2 found that structurally unsound (a column position is shared across whatever subunits currently occupy it, so ammo could regenerate for free under MB_CLOSE_RANKS=1 or silently stop being metered under MB_CLOSE_RANKS=0) and moved it to the Subunit/Unit ledger instead. And that a ranged kiter out of ammo would hold its wide standoff band forever, contributing nothing, since _kite_goal's far bound keyed on unit_type=='ranged' alone (F7; now also requires eff_volleys > 0, falling back to the melee reach bound once empty).

title: A8 executed: ROUT_CASCADE_FRAC chosen by sweep (0.6, corrected from an under-evidenced first choice of 0.5), goldens re-recorded
description: EXECUTION of ED-MB-0067 Part A's A8, the last Part-A item needing no ruling. config.py's own rule: 'chosen on evidence rather than asserted -- the sweep over candidate values is the experiment', targeting the repo's own 15-30% historical loser-casualty band (ED-MB-0031). Built systems/mass_battle/sim/workbench/rout_cascade_sweep.py (no prior sweep harness existed for this constant), driving tests/sim/gauge_mb.py's existing casualty_verdict()/LOSER_CAS_BAND machinery across candidate values, one subprocess per value (matching bat.py's/ci_golden_modes_check.py's established pattern for config toggles). THIS ROW'S FIRST DRAFT chose 0.5 and was adversarially reviewed (Opus, read-only) before being recorded, which found the row set was WRONG: it hand-listed six rows (H3/H4/H5/H6/H10/H11) and excluded C4/C7 on the unmeasured claim their losing side is always single-subunit. False -- C4/C7 build their _envelop_army side at pin_frac=2/3 (a 400/100/100 split), so the 400-troop centre alone reaches share 0.667, well above either candidate threshold; the exclusion criterion needed is 'does either side have >1 subunit', not a guess about who wins. FIXED by deriving the row set PROGRAMMATICALLY (any TESTS/CAV_TESTS row where gauge_mb.matchup's own a_is_fn/b_is_fn test is true for either side) instead of hand-curating it -- this cannot silently drop a row again. RE-RUN with the corrected 8-row set (H3/H4/H5/H6/H10/H11/C4/C7) at n=60 for the decision-relevant values (1.0 baseline, 0.7 plateau edge, 0.6, 0.5); full table committed at workbench/rout_cascade_sweep_results.json. RESULT, and why the choice changed: 1.0 and 0.7 are IDENTICAL across all 8 rows except C4/C7, which move slightly between them (different subunit-weight structure, still both far from the historical band); casualty-realism is 0/8 at both. At 0.6 AND 0.5, casualty-realism is IDENTICALLY 3/8 (H3/H10/C7 pass; the same three at both values) -- and 6 of 8 rows' raw numbers are IDENTICAL between 0.6 and 0.5 (H3/H4/H10/C4/C7). The ONLY difference between 0.6 and 0.5 is H5 and H6, both 2-body-weighted rows sitting near the exact-half boundary: H6's casualty realism improves further at 0.5 (43.1%->32.7%, still failing the band either way), but H5's WIN-SHARE regresses at 0.5 (51.0%->43.4%, exiting its 48-62 band) while staying inside its band at 0.6 (51.0% unchanged). 0.6 THEREFORE STRICTLY DOMINATES 0.5 on every measured dimension: identical casualty-realism gain, zero win-share-control cost versus 0.5's one-row cost. The earlier choice of 0.5 (matching the concept synthesis's own candidate, and CELL_BREAK_ROUT_FRAC's numeral) is not supported once win-share is checked as a control (CLAUDE.md Sec.0.1 pt 4) -- the 'identical methodology to CELL_BREAK_ROUT_FRAC' framing carried over from the concept synthesis was ALSO independently found false by the same review (CELL_BREAK_ROUT_FRAC's sibling weights by LIVE troops; this constant deliberately weights by SPAWN/start strength, per its own docstring's own reasoning for why a live weight would be wrong for the army-level ladder -- only the number and the >= comparison are shared, not the method) and is not repeated in this row. CAVEAT that survives whichever value is chosen, unchanged by the correction: Unit.derive_rout's cascade condition is PROVABLY INERT for any single-subunit Unit (a 0/1 step function clearing any threshold in (0,1] at the same instant) -- so massbattle.py:_faction_to_unit (the only function building Units for the live campaign, single-subunit per faction) is completely unaffected by this choice today; it starts mattering once a multi-subunit strategic army exists (A3's officers, ED-MB-0073, once wired to the campaign). GOLDENS: bat.py's own committed battery turns out NOT to move at 0.6 at all -- confirmed by direct re-run, not assumed: cell_field_mor0 and cell_legacy_mor1 both reproduce their ORIGINAL pre-A8 digests exactly at 0.6 (they DID move at the rejected 0.5, which is what the first draft re-recorded and this row reverts). tools/ci_golden_modes_check.py's FIELD_PINS re-pinned to '0.6' and re-verified [BYTE-EXACT OK] on all three of its modes. unit_legacy_mor0/cell_legacy_mor0 (test_mass_battle_byte_exact.py) shift again under 0.6 (a third distinct wrong value, following 1.0's original and 0.5's) -- still NOT re-recorded, since both already mismatch their EXPECTED for a separate, disclosed, pre-existing reason (ED-MB-0070/ED-MB-0061) this row does not investigate further. Suite shape unchanged throughout (xfail/skip, no new red). Sweep tool hardening from the same review: the worker now asserts the requested env value actually took effect (a silently-dropped override would otherwise read as 'identical to 1.0' -- indistinguishable from a real finding without the check); REPO ROOT is on sys.path unconditionally (the first version's documented direct-invocation usage would have raised ModuleNotFoundError, the same bootstrap bug ED-MB-0070 fixed in bat.py); every numeric literal in the script now carries a same-line [JUSTIFIED: ...] tag verified against tools/ci_sim_fabrication_check.py directly (the first draft's multi-line-spanning tags did not close on the same line and were silently uncited by the gate's own regex -- caught by running the actual tool, not by inspection). test_rout_contagion.py: test_default_is_inert (hardcoded the old default as an invariant) is test_threshold_1_0_is_inert (pins 1.0 explicitly, decoupled from the live default) plus test_shipped_default_is_no_longer_inert (now asserting 0.6) plus a new test_a_two_body_army_at_exactly_half_does_not_cascade_at_the_shipped_default pinning the exact-half boundary the review named as the untested hazard driving the H5/H6 sensitivity. Verified: engine/tests/ (sim-regression campaign goldens) re-run clean on the FINAL combined tree, after A3+C5 (ED-MB-0073) landed in the same working tree -- the review's own observation that A3+C5 shifted line numbers mid-review is addressed by re-running every check on the tree as it stands now, not the tree as it stood mid-review; every test file referencing ROUT_CASCADE_FRAC/derive_rout/_broken_share re-run directly and green.

title: A3+C5 executed: subordinate-officer Cmd / span-of-control (ED-1090's own queued reconciliation)
description: EXECUTION of A3 (ED-MB-0067 Part A) and C5 (Part C, ruled 2026-09-25: 'one ladder... max commanded = Command... at every echelon, including the new officer post'). This is the 'future ED' ED-1090 (2026-07-02) itself asked for: 'the ratified Command formula clamps to 1..7, so reaching [more than Command] commanded sub-units implies a future Command-exceeding mechanism (e.g. subordinate officers/lieutenancy) -- a future ED, not silently invented in the constructor.' NEW: Officer dataclass (hierarchy/units.py, beside Unit) -- name, command (default 4, the SAME tier-3 baseline build_army's own general parameter already uses -- deliberately NOT a new 'quality tier' table, since Part A's own text names one but C5 doesn't specify its magnitudes, and inventing numbers nothing ruled would be fabrication). Command derives via the SAME derive_command (ED-899, core/exchange.py) a Unit's own Command already uses when charisma+cognition are given -- no second formula one echelon down -- and clamps 1-7 identically. Subunit gains an `officer: Optional[str]` field (bookkeeping only, matching `role`'s own pre-Stage-D inert shape); Unit gains `officers: Tuple[Officer,...]`. build_army gains an `officers=()` parameter (default -- ZERO behavior change for every existing caller, verified: 39 tests/valoria files importing systems.mass_battle re-run clean, 322 passed/7 pre-existing KNOWN_RED xfails, no new failures) and a per-spec 'officer': NAME key. THE MECHANISM: when officers is empty, ED-1090's exact flat SUBUNIT_CAP=11 check runs unchanged (byte-identical error message, verified). When officers is given, that flat ceiling is REPLACED by C5's two-tier span-of-control ladder: each officer's own assigned-subunit count must be <= that officer's own Command, and the general's own direct reports (count of DISTINCT officers actually referenced + any un-officered/direct subunits) must be <= the general's own Command -- both checked eagerly at build_army construction time, raising ValueError on violation (matching the existing SUBUNIT_CAP-raise convention, not silent truncation). THIS IS WHAT LETS AN ARMY EXCEED SUBUNIT_CAP: a general with Command 3 fielding 3 officers of Command 4 each can field up to 12 subunits (3x4), properly distributed -- more than both the general's own Command and the old flat 11-subunit videogame ceiling. Verified against the exact 'Done when' criterion Part A specifies ('a general with Command c fields more than c sub-units through officers') by direct execution before writing tests, then pinned in tests/valoria/test_mass_battle_officers.py (11 tests: the positive scenario; both over-assignment failure modes -- an officer over their own Command, and a general over their own Command counting officers-plus-direct-reports; unknown-officer-name and duplicate-officer-name eager validation; Officer's own command derivation/default/clamp; officers passed as dicts or as Officer instances; and the officers=() backward-compatibility case verified byte-identical to the pre-A3 flat check). NOT DONE, disclosed rather than hidden: no upper ceiling was invented for the officered path (SUBUNIT_CAP simply does not apply once officers are used) -- Part A's own text specifies no replacement ceiling, and the existing deployment geometry (_centered_line_cols) already degrades (compresses) rather than crashes on an over-wide army, so this was not treated as a gap needing a new, un-ruled number. The concept's officer 'Steadiness contribution' (⌊Cmd/2⌋) is explicitly OUT of scope here per Part A's own text ('belongs to C3, not here') and per C3's own ruling (Steadiness was not adopted as a name) -- not touched. Officers are not yet reachable from the live campaign, same caveat as the rest of A1-A4's command/perception/plan layer: _faction_to_unit builds a single, un-officered subunit per faction (Part A's own 'Sequenced' table already gates army-scale plans on A1-A4 landing first, which this item does not change).
source: Direct design, build and verification, 2026-09-27, alongside the rest of Tier-2 execution.
